text:
sara: Hey team, customer ACME reports missing admin_* audit events in their SIEM export. They can see events in the UI but exported files have gaps. Also seeing some `403` and `AccessDenied` in forwarder logs. Any ideas?

james: Is this the SIEM forwarder pipeline (Kinesis->Firehose->S3) or the ad-hoc audit S3 export? Can you paste run_id and a sample event_id?

sara: It's the SIEM forwarder. run_id 20260315-9. Forwarder logs show: `WARN: dropped events: 42` and `ERROR: PutObject failed: AccessDenied`. Attached small log excerpt.

maria: I've asked the customer for full logs and bucket policy. They also mentioned KMS key rotation last week.

oliver: @james @sara quick thought: did the KMS alias change during rotation? If the forwarder still signs for the old key but bucket requires SSE-KMS header, writes could be rejected.

james: Checking IAM/roles... forwarder role has `kms:Decrypt` for alias/redwood/audit. But Firehose is throwing `InvalidKMSKeyException` on some attempts. CloudTrail shows `PutObject` errors from our forwarder IPs.

devops-bot: deploy/forwarder v2.14 rolled at 2026-03-14T22:33Z (changelog: include-sse-header).

oliver: That release started adding explicit SSE-KMS headers in some paths; for back-compat we may still send non-SSE in others. If a customer's bucket enforces SSE-KMS, non-SSE PutObject calls get AccessDenied and the forwarder drops events.

sara: Customer S3 bucket policy denies `PutObject` when `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header is missing. That would match the AccessDenied behavior and explain gaps.

maria: But the customer says some events show up in the exported file and in SIEM, while others are missing. Why would some writes succeed?

kyla: From compliance: our export schema requires `encryption.kms_key_id` in the payload so downstream SIEM mapping can verify retention/encryption. If forwarder does not populate that field, SIEM ingestion rules might drop the record (schema_mismatch).

sara: Example failed payload (redacted):
```
{"event_id":"evt-123","type":"admin.user.create","payload":"...","encryption":{}}
```

james: Proposed repro steps: 1) rotate KMS key, 2) deploy forwarder v2.14, 3) configure customer S3 bucket with SSE-only PutObject requirement. Result: AccessDenied for non-SSE writes and forwarder drops + schema_mismatch for records without encryption metadata.

oliver: Short-term mitigations: 1) ask customer to relax bucket policy to allow our forwarder (by ARN/IP) while we patch; OR 2) roll back the header change in forwarder. Long-term: make forwarder always honor bucket SSE policies and emit `encryption.kms_key_id` and `encryption.algorithm` in exported JSON.

maria: I'll draft a support KB with the workaround and instructions to verify bucket policy and KMS alias. Also will request the exact ACLs the forwarder needs.

sara: Customer also asked whether events were permanently lost or can be backfilled from DB. Can we run a backfill?

oliver: Backfill possible but must be done with correct encryption metadata and within retention window. Need DBA window and infra coordination. I'll open an infra ticket to schedule backfill and ensure KMS headers are correct for the generated files.

kyla: Compliance note: if any events were written unencrypted (e.g., SSE disabled) and accessible before rotation, we need to review exposure. Any signs of successful unencrypted writes?

james: So far most failures are AccessDenied. A few PutObject successes lacked `encryption` metadata — need to enumerate those. No evidence yet of public exposure.

auditor-bot: Audit export job 20260316-05 completed with 98% success; 64 events flagged as `schema_mismatch` and 12 `put_failed:AccessDenied`.

maria: Creating incident ticket REDWOOD-INC-2026-224 and will assign to @oliver and @james. I'll communicate a temporary mitigation to customer: allow forwarder put from our service principal and we'll coordinate a backfill.

james: I will own the infra ticket to add SSE-KMS compatibility and include `encryption.kms_key_id` in payload. ETA: EOD Thu.

oliver: I'll start planning the backfill and coordinate with DBA. Also raising a follow-up to add dropped-event metrics and alerting in console so customers see gaps sooner.

sara: Thanks. I'll attach the run logs and missing event id list to the incident.

maria: Draft customer update ready, will send after infra confirms mitigation.

james: Thanks all :thumbsup:
